ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory FINTRAC-compliant KYC/KYB for all general partners, limited partners and UBOs, including screening against the United Nations Consolidated List, Canadian SEMA schedules, Criminal Code Part II.1 listed entities, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists (given USD Swift/TT payment rails), national and international PEP databases, adverse-media and source-of-funds review covering the Dried Goji Berry and Herbal Botanicals supply chain; enhanced due diligence is mandatory where any UBO is a PEP, regardless of the 25% threshold, and at the 25% ownership threshold in all cases. The composite operational banking AML risk tier for this file is Low_Risk_Standard.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - Registre des entreprises du Quebec, official portal at www.registrequebec.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Charter of the French Language, C.Q.L.R. c. C-11, mandates that the partnership name be in French. The statutory legal designation 'societe en commandite' or the abbreviation 'S.E.C.' must be used; the English tokens 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.' are not accepted. Foreign names are permitted only if the name is a recognized trademark or the enterprise is otherwise exempt, and the French form or francisation of the name must appear in all registrations and commercial documents.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A REQ name reservation may be extended once for a further 60-day period by filing a written extension request before the original expiry. Upon rejection, the applicant should immediately reserve two or three alternative French-language names to preserve filing priority, file a formal written request for reconsideration (reexamen) with REQ within 30 days of the refusal, and, if the reconsideration is denied, initiate judicial review before the Court of Quebec under articles 523-529 of the Code of Civil Procedure within 30 days of the final notification.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. A Quebec societe en commandite must maintain a physical street address in Quebec for the head office (siege) and for service of process; a post-office box alone is impermissible. A virtual office operated by a licensed corporate service provider with a real Quebec premises, physical mail handling and acceptance of service is acceptable for this low-risk wholesale export business, but the partnership must maintain books and records, a resident general partner or agent, and sufficient commercial substance to sustain the passive passthrough classification for Canadian tax purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 12% - quantified first-year probability of an unannounced on-site inspection. The REQ does not conduct routine premises audits; however, the Canada Revenue Agency and Revenu Quebec may perform unannounced GST/QST and income-tax field visits, and the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) may conduct unannounced inspections of storage and export premises under the Safe Food for Canadians Act if the dried botanical products are shipped through CFIA-regulated channels.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP), Québec
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA Report (Category C/Declaration) under Règlement relatif à l'évaluation et l'examen des impacts sur l'environnement (Q-2, r. 23): dry-warehouse wholesale activity does not trigger the mandatory review procedure; a simple municipal zoning/environmental declaration may apply. No waste-water discharge or air emissions from production processes.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Municipal sanitary sewer bylaw compliance where applicable (pH 5.5-11.5; TSS ≤ 600 mg/L; BOD5 ≤ 500 mg/L; fats, oils and grease ≤ 150 mg/L); solid waste and packaging recycling under the Québec Residual Materials Regulation; no VOC or ozone-depleting substance releases; ambient noise compliant with municipal noise bylaw.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html, administering federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) and federal income tax. Quebec: Revenu Québec at https://www.revenuquebec.ca, administering the Quebec Sales Tax (QST), Quebec provincial income tax and, under a federal-provincial collection agreement, the federal GST charged in Quebec. Registry: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) at https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca, issuing the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) and registering the limited partnership.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Register the LP with REQ to obtain the 10-digit NEQ and statutory declaration of registration; 2) apply through the Business Registration Online (BRO) portal or Revenu Québec single window for a 15-character CRA Business Number (BN) with GST/HST program account 'RT' and QST account 'NR'; add payroll account 'RP' if employees are hired; 3) for a non-resident partner, submit CRA Form NR6 or equivalent where the partner elects net-basis taxation on Canadian rental/business income and provide the partner's foreign tax identification number; 4) file annual partnership information returns: T5013 (federal) and Relevé 15 / C0-500S (Quebec), allocating income, losses and credits to each partner; 5) open a Canadian bank account for CAD settlement and keep all SWIFT/TT remittance records as part of export substantiation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. Under the Income Tax Act (Canada) and the Taxation Act (Quebec), a limited partnership is fiscally transparent: it files information returns but pays no income tax; each partner reports its proportionate share. Territorial scope for non-resident partners: they are taxable in Canada on Canadian-source partnership income and are generally deemed to carry on business in Canada through the LP's Canadian permanent establishment; treaty relief does not displace Canadian taxing rights where the LP has a PE in Quebec. For GST/QST, the LP is a distinct 'person' and registrant, and is the taxpayer responsible for collecting and remitting indirect taxes on its supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box regime; entity classification follows the LP's legal form. Relevant elections: (1) voluntary GST/HST registration by a small supplier under Excise Tax Act subsection 240(3), with a mirror QST election; (2) section 216(1) ITA election by a non-resident partner to pay Part I net-basis tax on Canadian rental income instead of Part XIII gross withholding; (3) quick method of accounting election under ETA section 230 and corresponding QST provision; (4) annual filing/remittance election for eligible registrants with taxable supplies below CAD 1.5 million; (5) hybrid mismatch rules (BEPS Action 2, effective 1 July 2022) deny deductions for cross-border payments to an opaque foreign partner if not timely included in income, with no elective alignment mechanism available in Canada.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Dual-stack indirect tax: federal GST at 5% charged on taxable supplies in Quebec, plus provincial QST at 9.975% effective rate, both administered by Revenu Québec under the Excise Tax Act (Canada) and the Quebec Sales Tax Act.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000: the small-supplier threshold for both GST and QST, exceeded when worldwide taxable supplies (including zero-rated export sales) made by the LP and its associates reach CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or across four consecutive calendar quarters. Registration is mandatory within 30 days after the quarter in which the threshold is exceeded; zero-rated exports count as taxable supplies for this calculation, so an export-only wholesaler must register once invoice volumes cross the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API invoice stamping, or digital stamping exists in Canada or Quebec. The Pan-Canadian e-invoicing framework uses the Peppol PINT standard on a voluntary B2B/B2G basis. Revenu Québec accepts EDI, XML/EDIFACT, PDF and Peppol formats; GST/HST returns must be filed electronically via CRA NETFILE/XML or Revenu Québec CLICK/EDI for registrants. The LP should retain machine-readable export invoices to satisfy overseas customers' fiscal clearance requirements, but no government-side validation is required for goji berry export sales.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to supplies of tangible personal property (dried goji berries and herbal botanicals) sold in Quebec and physically exported, under the zero-rating provisions of the Excise Tax Act (Schedule VI, Part V) and the Quebec Sales Tax Act (mirror schedules). Conditions: (1) the LP transfers ownership to a non-resident buyer or ships goods to an address outside Canada; (2) the goods are delivered by the LP, its carrier, or a common carrier to an export destination; (3) the LP retains contemporaneous documentary proof of export available upon CRA or Revenu Québec audit. Related services supplied to a non-resident in respect of the exported goods are also zero-rated when performed for a non-resident client. The LP must be a GST/QST registrant to claim input tax credits (ITCs) and Quebec input tax refunds (ITRs) on purchases of organic goji berries and packaging, preserving the zero-rated chain.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency B13A or Canadian Export Reporting System CERS electronic record; mandatory for goods exceeding CAD 2,000 in value)
Commercial Invoice and Detailed Packing List
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing delivery outside Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank SWIFT/TT credit advice or foreign exchange confirmation showing export proceeds received)
Certificate of Origin and phytosanitary certificate where required by the importer's jurisdiction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess within the normal 4-year limitation period, extended indefinitely where misrepresentation or fraud exists. If export documentation is inadequate, the 0% rate is reversed and the LP is assessed 5% GST plus 9.975% QST on gross export revenues, with prescribed-rate daily compound interest. False statements or omissions carry a federal penalty of the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the omitted tax (Excise Tax Act section 285) and a Quebec penalty up to 50% of the tax (Quebec Tax Administration Act). Criminal tax evasion prosecution can result in fines up to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment. Retrospective clawbacks also disallow associated ITCs/ITRs, effectively taxing the full export margin.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as monetary, payments-system, and retail-payments regulator; financial institutions regulated by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, and FX-transaction reporting administered by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC). Canada maintains no dedicated foreign-exchange control authority; emergency exchange-control powers rest with the Minister of Finance under the Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada is an IMF Article VIII jurisdiction with full current-account and capital-account convertibility; there are no exchange controls, prior approvals, or repatriation licensing gates on capital inflows, trade settlements, profit distributions, or partnership redemptions. A Quebec limited partnership (société en commandite, CA_LP) may freely remit proceeds to non-resident limited partners; the only procedural hurdles are tax-compliance gates: Part XIII withholding at 25% statutory rate (treaty-reduced, commonly 15% for US/Chinese residents) on specified passive payments such as interest, rents, royalties, and management fees; Part XIV registration and reporting for non-resident partners carrying on business in Canada; and FINTRAC thresholds including CAD 10,000 reporting on large cash and virtual-currency transactions. No capital immobility or dividend-blocking rules apply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canadian law imposes no surrender of export proceeds, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory repatriation timeline for export receipts. The exporter may retain USD, EUR, or CNY balances in Canadian multi-currency accounts indefinitely, and conversion to CAD is optional at interbank market rates. Obligations are limited to accurate accrual-basis recognition for income-tax purposes, CFIA/export documentation for dried botanical products, and FINTRAC reporting of specified large transactions. The Canadian dollar floats freely under a market-determined exchange-rate regime; the Bank of Canada may intervene only in exceptional disorderly conditions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
Banque Nationale du Canada - Corporate and Trade Finance Desk

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low standalone feasibility. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., EEA or UK e-money institutions) are not deposit-taking institutions under the Bank Act and cannot lawfully maintain Canadian-based client accounts or issue CAD IBANs. A foreign EMI serving Canadian clients must register as a money services business (MSB) with FINTRAC, and providers operating on Canadian clearing and payment rails must be registered under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), administered by the Bank of Canada. The practical route is a sponsorship arrangement: partner with National Bank of Canada, BMO, or a Canadian-regulated MSB clearing agent that provides segregated settlement through a Tier 1 bank. Feasibility rating: Medium when used solely as a disbursement rail with a Canadian sponsor; Low as a standalone treasury or capital-holding rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors are not the operative capacity for a Quebec limited partnership; the general partner (commandité) must pass corporate KYC, and all limited partners are screened and named in the partnership register. FINTRAC permits entity identification remotely via the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) certified extract and digital identity proofing, including credit-bureau or video-based verification; physical attendance at a branch is therefore not statutorily required for a standard-risk wholesale exporter. In practice, National Bank, BMO, and Desjardins accept remote onboarding conditioned on a notarized certificate of incumbency, the REQ attestation, the executed partnership agreement, and a source-of-funds declaration; one video interview is commonly required for foreign-resident signatories. Physical presence may be imposed as an overlay bank policy where non-resident partner concentration exceeds 50% or where sanctions-sensitive counterparties are identified.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Layered ownership involving non-resident partnerships or discretionary trusts obscuring the 25% beneficial-ownership threshold.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed partnership agreement (contrat de société), REQ attestation de création, full register of limited partners with percentage interests, FINTRAC-compliant beneficial-ownership schedule, tax-residence certificates of all foreign partners, and economic-substance documentation such as Quebec office or warehouse lease, payroll records, and inventory evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered office is a virtual-address or tax-advisor location lacking demonstrable operational substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial lease or warehousing agreement in Quebec, utility statements, site photographs or video tour showing dried goji berry inventory, CFIA business licence for botanical export, and a notarized statutory declaration from the general partner confirming physical operations and management at that address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Supply-chain counterparties located in sanctioned, embargoed, or FATF high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Global Affairs Canada export permits, OSFI/FINTRAC sanctions-screening results for all buyers, end-user and country-of-final-destination declarations, Incoterms 2020 sales contracts, phytosanitary certificates, and a written trade-compliance policy evidencing denial-list and prohibited-party screening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media or politically exposed person (PEP) status of a limited partner or authorized signatory.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed PEP self-declaration, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements with supporting bank statements and capital-contribution wire records, statutory declaration of arm's-length relationship to public officials, and independent legal opinion confirming the absence of corruption indicators.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction pattern inconsistent with declared scope (ISIC 4631 / NAICS 424490 wholesale of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals), such as high-velocity payments to unrelated jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master wholesale supply agreement, commercial invoices with HS classification and Incoterms, bills of lading and customs export declarations, organic certification from an accredited body, CFIA phytosanitary permits, and a complete counterparty audit trail reconciliable to the declared business model.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident limited partners inject capital via SWIFT MT103 to the LP's domestic operating or capital-escrow account at a Quebec Schedule I bank. Compliant protocol: instruct remitting banks to state beneficiary account details at the Canadian bank, reference the REQ registration number and partnership agreement date, and use the purpose narrative 'Capital contribution - Quebec limited partnership (CA-QC)'. CAD-denominated flows clear through Lynx, Canada's real-time gross settlement system; USD flows clear via the bank's US correspondent (typically Fedwire). Pre-crediting verification by the receiving bank includes the general partner's resolution, partnership agreement excerpt, beneficiary-ownership attestation, and source-of-funds questionnaire. There is no Bank of Canada approval requirement, and contributed capital is not subject to GST/QST or Canadian withholding tax.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Export settlements for dried goji berries and botanical wholesale are executed on three rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 / MT202 for open-account transfers to credit-approved buyers, processed through Lynx and US correspondent networks; (ii) commercial documentary collections (DP/DA) under URC 522 with endorsed bills of lading for mid-risk counterparties; and (iii) irrevocable, confirmed letters of credit under UCP600 with a Canadian confirming bank for new or emerging-market buyers. Multi-currency account structures at National Bank, BMO, and RBC allow USD or EUR settlement without conversion; CNY payables are settled by FX conversion through correspondent banks because the Renminbi is not a Canadian clearing currency. FINTRAC reporting obligations apply to large cash and virtual-currency transactions, and a full audit trail of LCs, invoices, packing lists, phytosanitary certificates, and insurance documents must be retained.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD forward contracts (ISDA with Canadian CSA or Canadian Master Agreement; exempt from mandatory clearing as end-user hedging)
Plain-vanilla FX options (USD/CAD, EUR/CAD, and CNY/CAD calls and puts) offered by Schedule I Canadian banks
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for term-matched hedging of long-term partnership capital inflows

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing restricted currencies such as CNY/USD, permitted only for genuine trade-exposure hedging with an approved counterparty and a resolution of the general partner

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration pursuant to the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year-end Dec. 31: due no later than Jun. 1 of the following calendar year; non-calendar fiscal year-end: due no later than the day six months after the fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty is assessed under the Quebec legal publicity regime; after 12 months of non-filing, the Registraire des entreprises may cancel, revoke or strike the LP registration, triggering administrative dissolution and loss of standing in Quebec.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and associated schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Partnerships and Complex Entities Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a Dec. 31 fiscal year-end, due on or before Jun. 30 of the following calendar year; for any other fiscal year-end, due on the last day of the sixth month following the fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per month for each partner, for a minimum period of 12 months, with a maximum cap based on partnership membership; repeat or grossly negligent non-filing can trigger additional Income Tax Act penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No automatic statutory audit is imposed on a Quebec limited partnership for corporate purposes. An independent audit is mandatory when: (a) the LP is a reporting issuer or holds securities requiring registration with the Autorité des marchés financiers; (b) the LP operates in a federally regulated industry requiring financial statements; or (c) the partnership agreement, a lender, or the requisite majority of partners imposes an audit requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or Canadian ASPE per CPA Canada Handbook. A private limited partnership generally applies Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE); IFRS is required if the partnership is publicly accountable or is expressly required by securities law.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner must confirm changes to limited partner information on the Quebec annual declaration. Internally, the LP must maintain a complete beneficial-ownership ledger, record all partnership interest transfers, and obtain a written attestation from each partner at least annually for AML-CFT compliance. A transfer of partnership units is recorded only after the general partner approves the transfer and the assignee executes a supplementary agreement.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General Partner particulars and appointments
Minute Book of general partner resolutions and limited partner consents
UBO register containing beneficial owners, capital contributions, and transfer history

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 8,000–18,000 for a mandatory independent audit; 3,000–7,000 for a review engagement where no statutory audit is triggered
